text:
sarah_support: Escalation from ACME — streaming responses intermittently stop after ~40-70s idle, client reconnects, sometimes partial JSON chunking. Customer says repeated reconnects are causing duplicated token charges. They included a repro curl and headers.

sarah_support: Repro curl they gave: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=rw-13b\"`

sarah_support: Their client sees a final chunk like `data: {"choices": [{"delta": {}}]}` then connection FIN and partial last token. Connection closed by LB according to their network team.

jon_sre: Thanks — have you got the x-request-id from the root request? need to correlate with edge logs. ALB commonly kills idle connections at 60s by default, Cloudflare has 100s but may send RST on half-close. Could be probe/health-window interaction.

sarah_support: Sent logs to this thread, x-req ids included: `xr-1234abcd`. Customer traces show upstream code 200 then later `Connection: close` from loadbalancer.

marta_runtime: Quick note — our runtime will half-close the *server* side after sending final `\n\n`. If LB resets before client reads trailing buffered bytes, client gets truncated. Also note some proxies buffer until full chunk before flushing.

alex_support: Also the customer reported they route through Cloudflare Workers in front of ALB. CF has proxy buffering that can coalesce SSE unless `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` are preserved.

jon_sre: Repro suggestion: run from a host behind ALB to eliminate CF. Use `socat` or `nc` to observe TCP FIN timing: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w sse.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` then `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -quiet` and issue raw request. Look for `FIN, ACK` from LB within idle window.

marta_runtime: Workaround we can offer immediately: enable heartbeat comment frames every 15s from runtime to keep some bytes flowing: `: keepalive\n\n` — many proxies will not close an active connection that sees periodic traffic. We can push a small config flag per-customer (keepalive_interval).

jon_sre: Longer term: recommend customer increase ALB idle timeout to 300+ seconds if they can. ALB default 60s; set to 350s if chat sessions go long. For Cloudflare, set `origin_keepalive_timeout` and disable buffering for that route.

sarah_support: Customer concerned re billing: duplicated reconnects cause multiple partial token charges. Can billing team de-dupe rapid reconnects <2s? Otherwise advise customer to resume rather than reopen session.

alex_support: Filed a support followup to billing (INC-9876) asking for a reconciliation window and potential credits. Added note to suggest session resume logic client-side.

jon_sre: I'll collect matching edge/proxy logs for xr-1234abcd and run pcap. If we confirm LB->RST at ~65s we can mark as ALB idle timeout. If it's 30s it's likely Cloudflare. If it's 1-2s after FIN from our side, then runtime half-close bug.

marta_runtime: I can push a canary build that emits keepalive comments and a small flush after each token to reduce buffering: config `sse.flush_after_token=true`. Canary id: canary-2026-03-17-01.

sarah_support: Great. Next steps for me: tell customer to try direct call (bypass CF) with `curl -N` and to share tcpdump if possible. Offer temporary token credit for duplicated charges while we triage.

jon_sre: I'll attach initial pcap and edge log snippets here when ready. tagging @incidents_bot to track.
